name: Search field
first: A field for the text the user searches for, which SwiftUI places in the toolbar of a navigation stack, and whose text is a binding that the view filters its data with.

dependsOn.why: SwiftUI places the search field in the toolbar of the navigation stack around the view.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The `Text` is inside a `NavigationStack`, as `list` is on the page of Navigation stack.

dependsOn.why: A search field writes the text the user types through a binding to a string.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The value `$query` is a binding to the state `query`, as `$nights` is a binding to `nights` on the page of Binding.

what.is: A search field is a field for the text that the user searches for. The modifier `searchable(text:)` adds one, with a binding to a string that holds the text, and SwiftUI places it in the toolbar of the navigation stack around the view. The view filters its data with that string.
what.afterExample: The view `Cities` shows the cities that contain the search text. When the text becomes Li, the `body` runs again, and shows only Lima and Lisbon.
what.problem: A long list is hard to look through. A search field lets the user type part of a name, and the view shows only what matches. The system draws the field, in the place that users expect on each platform.
what.how: Apple's documentation says that the modifier, on a navigation stack or a view inside one, makes a search field appear in the toolbar, and that it takes a binding to a string, whose storage the app provides. As the user types, the field writes the text through the binding. The `body` read that state, so it runs again, and filters with the new text.

when.text: Use it for a list that the user looks for items in, such as trips or cities.
Don't use it for a few items that fit on the screen. A short list is quicker to read than to search.

parts.name: The modifier `searchable(text:)`, line 13
parts.text: The modifier adds a search field to the toolbar of the navigation stack that the `Text` is in. It is given `$query`, a binding to the state `query`, where the field writes the text the user types.

parts.name: The search text `query`, line 4
parts.text: The state `query` holds the search text, and starts empty. Lines 7 to 9 keep the cities that contain it, or every city while it is empty.

steps.text: Line 18 makes a `Cities` and draws it. The state `query` starts empty.
The `body` runs. The state `query` is empty, so lines 7 to 9 keep every city, and line 10 prints {{shows ["Lima", "Oslo", "Lisbon"]}}.
The `Text` appears, and line 14 sets `query` to `"Li"`, as the search field would when the user types Li.
The `body` read `query`, so it runs again. Line 8 keeps the cities that contain Li, and line 10 prints {{shows ["Lima", "Lisbon"]}}.

end.text: The search text is state, so each change to it ran the `body` again, which filtered the cities with the new text.
